title: KV cache health: fragmentation/eviction/compaction dashboards + alert rules
author: Allison Grant
description:
Context
We’ve been chasing bursty p95/p99 latency spikes correlated with KV cache fragmentation + allocator churn in some hosted regions and a few Dedicated pools. As part of KV cache compaction improvements, we need a shared, opinionated “KV cache health” dashboard plus alert rules that SRE can use during canary and for ongoing detection of regressions.

This PR adds:
- Grafana dashboard: KV Cache Health (per region/pool/model_family) including fragmentation, eviction rate, compaction cost, allocation failures, and tail latency overlays.
- Prometheus/Mimir alert rules with recommended thresholds + canary-oriented signals (including “allocation failures present” as a hard stop).
- Documentation in-repo for panel intent, query notes, and rollup guidance.

Notes / assumptions
- Metric names are aligned to the runtime metrics introduced in redwood monorepo (see ENG-2842 / PR redwood#18423):
  - redwood_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio{region,pool,model_family}
  - redwood_kv_cache_alloc_failures_total{region,pool,model_family}
  - redwood_kv_cache_evictions_total{reason,region,pool,model_family}
  - redwood_kv_cache_compaction_gpu_ms_total{region,pool,model_family}
  - redwood_kv_cache_compaction_cpu_ms_total{region,pool,model_family}
  - redwood_kv_cache_compaction_bytes_moved_total{region,pool,model_family}
  - redwood_kv_cache_compaction_budget_exceeded_total{region,pool,model_family}
- All alerts are scoped to runtime pools and are intended to page SRE only when sustained (to avoid noise during expected burst windows). For canary, we will also watch the same panels with a shorter lookback.

Dashboard: “KV Cache Health”
Panels (high level)
1) Fragmentation
- Fragmentation ratio (p50/p90 across instances) by pool
- Fragmentation ratio heatmap by model_family
- “Fragmentation vs decode p99” overlay (optional panel used in canary)

2) Allocation / OOM pressure signals
- KV alloc failures (rate over 5m) (hard stop)
- KV cache “admission blocked due to cache pressure” (if present) and queue depth overlays (where available)

3) Eviction
- Evictions/sec split by reason (completed, ttl, pressure)
- Evictions/sec per tenant tier (where labels are available; otherwise aggregated)

4) Compaction cost
- Compaction GPU ms/s and CPU ms/s (rate)
- Bytes moved/s (rate)
- Budget exceeded events (rate)

5) Rollup and triage helpers
- Table: top pools by fragmentation_ratio (current + 1h max)
- Table: pools with alloc_failures in last 30m
- Links to runbook and perf-canary results

Recommended alert thresholds
These are tuned to detect regressions while keeping paging reasonable; we can tighten after canary if needed.

1) KV cache allocation failures (critical, page)
- Alert: RedwoodKVCacheAllocFailuresPresent
- Condition: increase(redwood_kv_cache_alloc_failures_total[5m]) > 0
- For: 0m (immediate)
- Rationale: alloc failures are strongly correlated with timeouts and are a clear rollback signal.

2) Fragmentation sustained high (warning + critical)
- Warning: RedwoodKVCacheHighFragmentation
  - Condition: avg_over_time(redwood_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio[15m]) > 0.28
  - For: 15m
- Critical: RedwoodKVCacheVeryHighFragmentation
  - Condition: avg_over_time(redwood_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio[10m]) > 0.35
  - For: 10m
- Rationale: above ~0.30 we’ve historically seen allocator churn and p99 sensitivity under burst mixes.

3) Compaction cost regression (warning)
- Alert: RedwoodKVCacheCompactionCostHigh
- Condition: (rate(redwood_kv_cache_compaction_gpu_ms_total[5m]) > 250) OR (rate(redwood_kv_cache_compaction_cpu_ms_total[5m]) > 400)
- For: 15m
- Rationale: budget drift and/or pathological move patterns; intended to catch compaction thrash before it hits p99.

4) Compaction budget exceeded (warning)
- Alert: RedwoodKVCacheCompactionBudgetExceeded
- Condition: rate(redwood_kv_cache_compaction_budget_exceeded_total[10m]) > 0
- For: 10m
- Rationale: indicates we’re hitting safety guardrails; should correlate with the scheduler “cache pressure” handling and potentially require tuning.

5) Eviction churn spike (warning)
- Alert: RedwoodKVCacheEvictionsHigh
- Condition: rate(redwood_kv_cache_evictions_total{reason="pressure"}[5m]) > 120
- For: 15m
- Rationale: eviction pressure spikes often precede fragmentation-induced tail issues; also helps catch mis-tuned cache limits.

Implementation details
- Adds dashboard JSON under dashboards/runtime/kv-cache-health.json and registers it in dashboards/index.yaml.
- Adds alert rules under alerts/runtime/kv-cache-health.yaml with runbook_url annotations.
- Adds README notes for operators about label expectations (region/pool/model_family) and how to interpret “GPU ms/s”.

Rollout / ops
- These dashboards/alerts are intended to ship before enabling compaction canary broadly (ENG-2851). During canary, SRE will use dashboard panels as primary stop/go along with tail latency SLO.
- Paging routes: alloc failures => page; the rest are warning-level and should land in #eng-sre-alerts unless we see persistent regressions.

References
- Linear: ENG-2850 (Observability dashboards), ENG-2842 (metrics), ENG-2851 (canary plan)
- Incident context: PM-2025-02-11 burst tail latency / KV fragmentation
- Related runtime work: redwood#18423 (metrics), perf-canary PR-388 (gating)

Screenshots
- Included in commit 3 as panel previews (Grafana export).

Testing
- Validated PromQL queries against staging Mimir with synthetic series.
- Imported dashboard into staging Grafana and verified templating for region/pool/model_family.
- Alert rule test: promtool test rules (added small golden tests for alloc_failures and fragmentation alerts).
commits: Add KV Cache Health dashboard (Grafana export + templating)
Register dashboard in observability-pack index + folder mapping
Add runtime alert rules for fragmentation / allocation failures / compaction cost
Add promtool tests for key alert expressions

review_conversation:
Aisha Bello (review): The fragmentation thresholds look reasonable, but can we avoid paging on warning by default? Also please add a note on why 0.28/0.35 were chosen.
Allison Grant (author): Yep—set warning rules to route to #eng-sre-alerts only; only alloc failures pages. Added rationale in the PR description + docs referencing historical burst mixes.

Sean Gallagher (review): For canary, we’ll want shorter “for” durations. Can we include suggested canary watch settings without changing prod alerts?
Allison Grant (author): Added docs section “Canary watch mode” with suggested ad-hoc queries (5m lookback) and a note to avoid committing shorter for-durations to main.

Logan Wright (review): Metric naming: ensure we’re using *_total counters everywhere and rate() them. Also confirm model_family label is present universally.
Allison Grant (author): Updated expressions to use rate()/increase() only on *_total. Added fallback notes in docs: if model_family missing in older pools, use model label or aggregate.

Omar El-Sayed (review): For compaction cost, GPU ms/s threshold might vary by model size; can we make it relative to token throughput?
Allison Grant (author): Good call. Added an additional panel “compaction GPU ms / 1k tokens decoded” (no alert for now). Kept absolute GPU ms/s alert as a broad thrash detector; we can revisit after first canary.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please include runbook_url annotation on every alert and confirm the alloc failure alert is a hard rollback signal.
Allison Grant (author): Added runbook_url everywhere + annotated alloc failures as rollback trigger; linked to the mitigation runbook section.

Final approvals: Aisha Bello, Sean Gallagher, Logan Wright. Omar El-Sayed approved with note to revisit compaction normalization after canary.
release_notes: Adds KV Cache Health Grafana dashboard and alert rules to detect fragmentation, allocation failures, eviction churn, and compaction cost regressions (used for compaction canary and ongoing monitoring).
